topic: The BraTS 2024 Post-Treatment Glioma (BraTS-GLI) segmentation challenge: tumor sub-region labels (ET, NETC, SNFH, RC) and the WT/TC/ET evaluation regions
overview:
The Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) challenge is a long-running international benchmark, held annually at the MICCAI conference since 2012, in which research teams compete to build algorithms that automatically outline brain tumors on MRI scans. Each patient is imaged with four standard MRI "sequences" — a plain T1 scan, a T1 scan taken after injecting gadolinium contrast (T1-Gd / T1c), a T2 scan, and a T2-FLAIR scan — because different parts of a tumor show up on different sequences. Historically BraTS focused on brand-new, untreated ("pre-operative") gliomas. The 2024 challenge (described by Correia de Verdier and colleagues, arXiv:2405.18368) was the first to tackle the much harder and more clinically common situation of imaging gliomas AFTER treatment — after surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy — using what the organizers describe as the largest expert-annotated post-treatment glioma dataset assembled (roughly 2,200 cases from seven institutions).

Post-treatment scans are messy: surgery leaves a fluid-filled hole (the resection cavity), radiation causes bright signal that mimics tumor, and "pseudoprogression" (treatment reaction that looks like tumor growth) confuses even expert radiologists. To capture this, BraTS 2024 defines four voxel-level labels: enhancing tissue/tumor (ET, label 3), non-enhancing tumor core (NETC, label 1), surrounding non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensity / edema (SNFH, label 2), and resection cavity (RC, label 4). These are the raw classes a model must predict for every voxel in the 3D volume.

Because clinicians care about anatomically meaningful compartments rather than the raw labels, models are scored not on the four labels directly but on three (in 2024, four) "evaluation regions" built by unioning labels: Enhancing Tumor (ET = label 3 alone), Tumor Core (TC = NETC + ET), and Whole Tumor (WT = NETC + SNFH + ET); RC is additionally evaluated on its own. This nested structure (ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT) mirrors how a radiologist thinks — from the active tumor outward to the full extent of abnormality.

Scoring uses two "lesion-wise" metrics: the lesion-wise Dice Similarity Coefficient (overlap agreement, 0 to 1) and the lesion-wise 95% Hausdorff Distance (boundary error in millimetres). "Lesion-wise" means each separate tumor focus is scored individually and then averaged, so a model gets no credit for nailing one big lesion while missing several small but clinically critical ones — a deliberate fix for the size bias of older, whole-image metrics.

key_points.point: BraTS 2024 is the first BraTS challenge to focus on POST-treatment (post-surgery/radiation/chemo) adult glioma MRI, whereas prior BraTS glioma tasks focused on pre-operative (untreated) tumors. It uses what the organizers call the largest expert-annotated post-treatment glioma dataset (~2,200 cases from seven institutions, split roughly 70% train / 10% validation / 20% test).
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 Challenge paper, arXiv:2405.18368

key_points.point: Four MRI sequences are provided per case: pre-contrast T1, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted (T1-Gd, also called T1c), T2-weighted, and T2-FLAIR. Different tumor components are defined by their appearance across these sequences.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper (arXiv HTML)

key_points.point: Enhancing Tissue/Tumor (ET) is defined as hyperintense (bright) signal on post-contrast T1-Gd after excluding blood vessels; thick or nodular enhancement counts as ET, but thin linear treatment-related enhancement along the resection cavity or dura is deliberately excluded. ET represents active tumor with a disrupted blood-brain barrier.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper (arXiv HTML)

key_points.point: Non-Enhancing Tumor Core (NETC) covers regions that appear dark on BOTH T1 and T1-Gd (necrosis/cysts), plus dark-on-T1-Gd regions that are brighter on T1 and are not otherwise a resection cavity. It captures the dead/cystic core of the tumor that does not take up contrast.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper (arXiv HTML)

key_points.point: Surrounding Non-enhancing FLAIR Hyperintensity (SNFH) is the T2/FLAIR bright abnormality around the tumor. In the post-treatment setting it lumps together several biologically distinct things: peritumoral edema, infiltrating non-enhancing tumor, radiation-related change, and gliosis — the model is not asked to separate these.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper (arXiv HTML)

key_points.point: Resection Cavity (RC) is the post-surgical bed left after tumor removal — fluid-, air-, blood-, or protein-filled. Chronic cavities (typically >3-6 months old) are isointense to cerebrospinal fluid on both T1 and T2/FLAIR. RC is a NEW label unique to the post-treatment challenge and is absent from pre-operative BraTS tasks.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper (arXiv HTML)

key_points.point: The integer label encoding in the released segmentation masks is: 1 = NETC, 2 = SNFH, 3 = ET, 4 = RC (0 = background). These are mutually exclusive per-voxel classes.

Evaluation is done on nested composite regions, not the raw labels: Enhancing Tumor ET = {label 3}; Tumor Core TC = NETC ∪ ET = {labels 1,3}; Whole Tumor WT = NETC ∪ SNFH ∪ ET = {labels 1,2,3}. This gives the containment hierarchy ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT. Note WT does NOT include the resection cavity (label 4).
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper; BraTS2024_Task1.md

key_points.point: In the 2024 post-treatment challenge the resection cavity (RC) is scored as its own fourth evaluation region in addition to ET, TC, and WT, so competitors are ranked on four regions.

Performance is measured with two lesion-wise metrics: the lesion-wise Dice Similarity Coefficient (overlap, higher is better, range 0-1) and the lesion-wise 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95, boundary error in mm, lower is better). 'Lesion-wise' scores each connected lesion separately then averages, so small missed lesions are not hidden by one large correct one.
key_points.source: Correia de Verdier et al., BraTS 2024 paper; Official BraTS-2023 Metrics repo (rachitsaluja)

key_points.point: The lesion-wise algorithm dilates the ground-truth labels and runs 26-connectivity 3D connected-component analysis to identify individual lesions; each predicted false-positive lesion and each missed false-negative lesion is assigned a Dice of 0 (and a large HD95 penalty), and the case score is the mean over all true-positive, false-positive, and false-negative lesions.

The clinical motivation for a dedicated post-treatment task is that treated gliomas produce pseudoprogression (new/increasing enhancement that later subsides without therapy change) and radiation change that mimic true tumor; the RANO 2.0 criteria were developed precisely to standardize post-treatment response assessment because older Macdonald criteria overdiagnosed progression.

Pseudoprogression frequency in glioblastoma cohorts following chemoradiotherapy has been reported in the ~13-24% range, underscoring why distinguishing true tumor from treatment effect on post-treatment MRI is difficult and clinically consequential.
key_points.source: Radbruch et al., pseudoprogression / RANO evaluation, PMC3755387

key_points.point: BraTS has run annually at MICCAI since 2012 and standardized the clinical nomenclature and multi-institutional mpMRI benchmarking that underpins the 2024 post-treatment task; by 2023 it had expanded to metastases, meningioma, pediatric tumors, and sub-Saharan populations.
key_points.source: Advancing Precision: Review of BraTS MRI Segmentation Datasets 2012-2025, Sensors (MDPI), PMC11945730

equations.name: Dice Similarity Coefficient (set form)
equations.variables_explained: P is the set of voxels the model predicts as belonging to a region; G is the ground-truth (expert) set of voxels for that region; |·| is the number of voxels (cardinality); |P ∩ G| is the number of voxels in both. DSC ranges from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (perfect overlap).

equations.name: Dice in confusion-matrix form
equations.variables_explained: TP (true positives) = voxels correctly predicted as the region; FP (false positives) = voxels predicted as the region but not in the ground truth; FN (false negatives) = ground-truth voxels the model missed. This is algebraically identical to the set form.

equations.name: Dice as harmonic mean of precision and recall
equations.variables_explained: Precision is the fraction of predicted region voxels that are correct; Recall (sensitivity) is the fraction of true region voxels that were found. Dice equals their harmonic mean, so it punishes imbalance between the two.

equations.name: Evaluation-region composition from labels
equations.variables_explained: Labels are 1=NETC, 2=SNFH, 3=ET, 4=RC. A voxel belongs to an evaluation region if its label is in that region's set. The nesting ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT holds because each larger region is a superset. RC (label 4) is scored separately and is not part of WT.

equations.name: 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95)
equations.variables_explained: ∂P and ∂G are the surface (boundary) voxels of the prediction and ground truth; d(p,G) is the distance from boundary point p to the nearest ground-truth boundary point; P_95{·} takes the 95th percentile of that set of distances. Taking the 95th percentile instead of the strict maximum makes the metric robust to a few outlier voxels. Lower HD95 = better boundary agreement (mm).

equations.name: Lesion-wise Dice (per case)
equations.variables_explained: N_TP = number of correctly detected ground-truth lesions (each contributes its own Dice_i); N_FP = number of spurious predicted lesions (each scored 0); N_FN = number of missed ground-truth lesions (each scored 0). Dividing by the total lesion count spreads the penalty over every detection error, so missing small lesions lowers the score even if the detected lesion is segmented well.

derivations.title: Deriving the confusion-matrix form of Dice from the set form (with numbers)
steps: \mathrm{DSC} = \dfrac{2\,|P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|} — Start from the definition: twice the overlap divided by the sum of the two set sizes. P = predicted voxels, G = ground-truth voxels.
|P \cap G| = \mathrm{TP} — The overlap (voxels in both P and G) is exactly the true positives, by definition of TP.
|P| = \mathrm{TP} + \mathrm{FP} — Every predicted voxel is either also in the ground truth (TP) or not (FP); these are disjoint and exhaust P.
|G| = \mathrm{TP} + \mathrm{FN} — Every ground-truth voxel is either found by the model (TP) or missed (FN); these are disjoint and exhaust G.

\mathrm{DSC} = \dfrac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP})+(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN})} = \dfrac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}} — Substitute the three equalities and collect the two TP terms in the denominator. This is the confusion-matrix form.

\text{Numeric check: } \mathrm{TP}=80,\ \mathrm{FP}=10,\ \mathrm{FN}=20 \Rightarrow \mathrm{DSC}=\dfrac{2(80)}{2(80)+10+20} — Plug in concrete voxel counts: the model correctly labels 80 region voxels, wrongly adds 10, and misses 20.
\mathrm{DSC} = \dfrac{160}{160+30} = \dfrac{160}{190} \approx 0.842 — Evaluate: the model scores about 0.84 Dice for this region. Perfect would be 1.0.

derivations.title: Showing Dice is the harmonic mean of precision and recall
steps: \mathrm{Precision} = \dfrac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}}, \quad \mathrm{Recall} = \dfrac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN}} — Definitions: precision = fraction of predictions that are correct; recall = fraction of truth that is captured.

\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{Precision}} + \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{Recall}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}}{\mathrm{TP}} + \dfrac{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN}}{\mathrm{TP}} — Take reciprocals of each and prepare to add (the harmonic mean works with reciprocals).

\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{Precision}} + \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{Recall}} = \dfrac{(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP})+(\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN})}{\mathrm{TP}} = \dfrac{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}{\mathrm{TP}} — Add the fractions over the common denominator TP and combine the numerators.

\text{Harmonic mean} = \dfrac{2}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{Precision}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{Recall}}} = \dfrac{2}{\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}{\mathrm{TP}}} — The harmonic mean of two numbers is 2 divided by the sum of their reciprocals; substitute the sum from the previous step.

= \dfrac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}} = \mathrm{DSC} — Invert the compound fraction (multiply numerator and denominator by TP). The result is exactly the Dice formula, proving Dice = harmonic mean of precision and recall.

derivations.title: Building WT, TC, ET voxel counts from the four labels (worked example)
steps: \text{Given per-voxel label counts: } n_{NETC}=100,\ n_{SNFH}=500,\ n_{ET}=200,\ n_{RC}=150 — Suppose the ground-truth mask of one case has these voxel counts for labels 1,2,3,4 respectively. Labels are mutually exclusive, so a voxel has exactly one.
\mathrm{ET}_{\text{count}} = n_{ET} = 200 — The Enhancing Tumor evaluation region is label 3 alone, so its size is just the ET count.
\mathrm{TC}_{\text{count}} = n_{NETC} + n_{ET} = 100 + 200 = 300 — Tumor Core = NETC ∪ ET. Because the labels are disjoint, the union's size is the sum of the two counts.
\mathrm{WT}_{\text{count}} = n_{NETC} + n_{SNFH} + n_{ET} = 100 + 500 + 200 = 800 — Whole Tumor = NETC ∪ SNFH ∪ ET. Again disjoint labels, so just add. Note the resection cavity (150) is NOT added.
\mathrm{RC}_{\text{count}} = n_{RC} = 150 — Resection Cavity is evaluated as its own region (label 4), separate from WT/TC/ET.
\mathrm{ET}(200) \le \mathrm{TC}(300) \le \mathrm{WT}(800) — Sanity check: the nested containment ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT is reflected in non-decreasing voxel counts, as expected.

derivations.title: Why lesion-wise Dice differs from global Dice (worked example)
steps: \text{Case has 3 true lesions; model detects 2, misses 1, and adds 1 false lesion.} — Set up: N_TP=2, N_FN=1, N_FP=1. Two detected lesions have per-lesion Dice 0.90 and 0.80; the missed and spurious lesions score 0.

\overline{\mathrm{DSC}}_{\text{lesion}} = \dfrac{\mathrm{DSC}_1 + \mathrm{DSC}_2 + 0_{FN} + 0_{FP}}{N_{TP}+N_{FN}+N_{FP}} — Apply the lesion-wise formula: sum the per-lesion Dice values (missed and false lesions contribute 0) and divide by the total lesion count.
= \dfrac{0.90 + 0.80 + 0 + 0}{2+1+1} = \dfrac{1.70}{4} = 0.425 — Substitute: the model's lesion-wise Dice is only 0.425, heavily penalized for the missed and spurious lesions.

\text{Contrast: if the 2 detected lesions are large and the missed one is tiny, a GLOBAL (voxel-pooled) Dice might be } \approx 0.88 — Pooling all voxels together lets big correct lesions dominate, hiding the missed small lesion — exactly the size bias lesion-wise scoring is designed to remove.
\Delta = 0.88 - 0.425 = 0.455 — The gap quantifies how much the lesion-wise metric penalizes clinically important detection failures that a global metric would mask.

intuitions: Think of the four labels as the raw paint colors a model must assign to every voxel, and the evaluation regions (WT/TC/ET) as the meaningful shapes you get by mixing those colors. Radiologists don't act on 'label 3' — they act on 'how much active tumor is there' (ET), 'how big is the tumor's solid core' (TC), and 'how far does the abnormality extend' (WT). The union-based regions translate machine labels into clinical questions.

The regions are like Russian nesting dolls: ET (active enhancing tumor) sits inside TC (core = enhancing + dead/cystic tissue), which sits inside WT (core + surrounding FLAIR abnormality). Scoring the nested regions rather than the raw labels also makes the metric more forgiving of the fuzzy, subjective boundaries between adjacent tissue types that even experts disagree on.

The post-treatment setting is fundamentally about ambiguity: after surgery and radiation, a bright spot on MRI could be regrowing tumor, dead tissue, scar, or a treatment reaction (pseudoprogression). The RC label and the deliberate exclusion of thin linear post-surgical enhancement from ET are the challenge's way of encoding 'this looks like tumor but is really treatment effect' so models don't cry wolf.

Lesion-wise scoring reflects a clinical value judgment: a new 4 mm nodule that a model misses can change a patient's treatment as much as a large mass. By scoring every lesion separately and giving a zero for each miss or false alarm, the metric refuses to let a model hide small but decisive errors behind one big, well-segmented lesion.
gotchas: Whole Tumor (WT) does NOT include the resection cavity. WT = NETC ∪ SNFH ∪ ET (labels 1,2,3); RC (label 4) is excluded from WT and scored as its own region. It is easy to wrongly assume 'whole' means 'everything abnormal.'

ET means two different things depending on context. As a raw label it is 'enhancing tissue = label 3'; as an evaluation region it is also just label 3 — so here they coincide. But do not confuse the label NETC ('non-enhancing tumor CORE', label 1) with the region TC ('tumor core' = labels 1+3). NETC is a subset of TC, not the same thing.

Not all bright FLAIR signal is tumor. SNFH deliberately merges edema, infiltrating tumor, radiation change, and gliosis into one label — the challenge does not ask the model to tell these apart, so a high SNFH Dice does not mean the model distinguished true tumor from treatment effect.

Thin linear enhancement along the resection cavity or dura is treatment-related and is intentionally excluded from ET, even though it is bright on T1-Gd. A model that greedily labels all post-contrast brightness as ET will over-segment and be penalized.

Lesion-wise Dice is not the same number as the classic 'global' voxel-overlap Dice reported in older BraTS papers. A single missed small lesion or one false-positive blob is scored as a full 0 and averaged in, so lesion-wise scores are typically lower and are NOT directly comparable to pre-2023 whole-image Dice values.

The paper text describes three tumor compartments (ET, NETC, SNFH); the resection cavity (RC) as a scored fourth evaluation region was added around the challenge release, so some early write-ups list only WT/TC/ET. Confirm whether a given result includes RC before comparing leaderboards.

example_questions.question: A model's prediction for one case has the following voxel counts by label: NETC (1) = 50, SNFH (2) = 300, ET (3) = 120, RC (4) = 90. The expert ground truth has NETC = 40, SNFH = 320, ET = 150, RC = 100. Assuming for simplicity that the predicted and true voxels for each label overlap as much as possible, compute the Tumor Core (TC) voxel counts for prediction and ground truth, and give the best-case Dice for TC.
example_questions.answer: Step 1 — TC region = NETC ∪ ET = labels 1 and 3. Prediction TC count = 50 + 120 = 170 voxels. Ground-truth TC count = 40 + 150 = 190 voxels. Step 2 — 'Overlap as much as possible' means the smaller set sits entirely inside the larger, so TP = min(170,190) = 170, FP = 170 − 170 = 0, FN = 190 − 170 = 20. Step 3 — Apply Dice = 2·TP / (2·TP + FP + FN) = 2(170) / (2·170 + 0 + 20) = 340 / (340 + 20) = 340/360 ≈ 0.944. So the best-achievable TC Dice for this case is about 0.94, limited by the 20 core voxels the model under-predicts.

example_questions.question: In one patient the ground truth contains 4 separate enhancing-tumor lesions. A model correctly finds 3 of them with per-lesion Dice scores of 0.95, 0.70, and 0.60, misses the 4th entirely, and also produces 2 false-positive enhancing blobs where there is no tumor. Compute the lesion-wise Dice for the enhancing-tumor region for this case.
example_questions.answer: Step 1 — Count lesion categories: true positives N_TP = 3 (the found lesions), false negatives N_FN = 1 (the missed lesion), false positives N_FP = 2 (the spurious blobs). Total lesions in the denominator = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6. Step 2 — Missed and spurious lesions each score 0. Numerator = 0.95 + 0.70 + 0.60 + 0 (FN) + 0 (FP) + 0 (FP) = 2.25. Step 3 — Lesion-wise Dice = 2.25 / 6 = 0.375. Interpretation: although the three detected lesions averaged (0.95+0.70+0.60)/3 = 0.75 on their own, the single miss and two false alarms drag the lesion-wise score down to 0.375, illustrating how the metric punishes detection errors, not just boundary sloppiness.

example_questions.question: Why does BraTS 2024 evaluate the nested regions WT, TC, and ET instead of directly scoring the four raw labels (NETC, SNFH, ET, RC)? Give both a clinical and a methodological reason.
example_questions.answer: Clinical reason: physicians make decisions on anatomically meaningful compartments, not on arbitrary label integers. 'Enhancing tumor' (ET) tracks active, blood-brain-barrier-disrupted tumor and is the quantity RANO response criteria emphasize; 'tumor core' (TC = enhancing + non-enhancing necrotic/cystic core) captures the solid tumor burden; 'whole tumor' (WT = core + surrounding FLAIR abnormality) captures the full extent of disease. Scoring these directly answers the questions clinicians actually ask. Methodological reason: the boundaries between adjacent raw labels (e.g., where SNFH edema ends and NETC begins, or infiltrating tumor vs. radiation change within SNFH) are subjective and experts disagree, so raw per-label Dice would be noisy and unfair. Unioning labels into nested regions (ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT) cancels many of those internal boundary disagreements — a voxel misassigned between NETC and ET still lands correctly inside TC and WT — yielding a more stable, reproducible benchmark. (In 2024 RC is additionally scored on its own because the resection cavity is a distinct, clinically important post-surgical structure.)

suggested_figures: A single axial post-treatment MRI slice shown in the four sequences (T1, T1-Gd, T2, FLAIR) side by side, with the four color-coded labels overlaid (NETC=blue, SNFH=green, ET=yellow, RC=red), annotated to show which sequence makes each label visible (e.g., ET bright on T1-Gd, SNFH bright on FLAIR, RC dark/CSF-like on both).

A nested Venn/onion diagram showing the label-to-region mapping: an innermost ET circle inside TC (ET + NETC) inside WT (ET + NETC + SNFH), with RC drawn as a separate detached region, plus the label integers (1,2,3,4) annotated — visually conveying ET ⊆ TC ⊆ WT and that RC is scored separately.

A schematic contrasting global (voxel-pooled) Dice vs. lesion-wise Dice on a cartoon brain with one large correctly-segmented lesion and two small missed lesions, showing the high global score next to the much lower lesion-wise score, to make the size-bias fix intuitive.
confidence_notes: Label integer encoding (1=NETC, 2=SNFH, 3=ET, 4=RC) was confirmed from the BraTS 2023/2024 solutions documentation (andre-fs-ferreira GitHub) and is consistent with BraTS conventions, but I did not see the integer values stated verbatim inside the arXiv HTML I retrieved — the arXiv paper defines the labels by name/appearance rather than by integer in the section I fetched. The WT/TC/ET union composition (WT=1,2,3; TC=1,3; ET=3) is confirmed from both the arXiv paper text ('Tumor Core = ET + NETC', 'Whole Tumor = ET + SNFH + NETC') and the solutions doc. Dataset size is reported as ~2,200 cases / seven institutions from the arXiv HTML fetch; the abstract's exact headline count may be phrased differently ('largest') and I did not re-verify a precise N against the published abstract line-by-line. The exact numeric HD95 penalty assigned to false-positive/false-negative lesions (some BraTS implementations use a fixed value such as 374 mm) was NOT confirmed from the sources I retrieved — the metrics repo confirms FP/FN get a 0 Dice and a penalized HD95 and case-mean averaging, but I could not verify the specific penalty constant, so I left it general. Pseudoprogression frequency (~13-24%) is from a specific GBM chemoradiotherapy cohort (PMC3755387) and should be read as cohort-dependent, not a universal figure. RANO 2.0 is cited for the general clinical rationale (post-treatment response assessment, pseudoprogression) and is contextual background, not a claim made by the BraTS paper itself. Per-lesion Dice/HD95 threshold details (e.g., dilation radius, minimum lesion volume to count) exist in the official metrics code but were summarized from the repo description rather than line-by-line from source.
